trainers.instruction: This picture shows a typical bar graph. Select three out of the five bars to see an example of how you can use a bar graph.

atoms.text: This graph shows five different modes of transportation and how fast they are. Each bar represents a different mode of transportation.

example.a: For example, the second bar shows the speed of the horse. The taller the bar, the faster it is.
example.sound: For example, the second bar shows the speed of the horse. The taller the bar, the faster it is.

atoms.a: Select the bar that shows the speed of a car.
Select the bar that shows the speed of a train.
Select the bar that shows the fastest mode of transportation.
Select the bar that shows the slowest mode of transportation.
Select the bar that is faster than walking, but slower than going by car.

instruction.text: Listen and read along, then select the correct answer by using the information from the graph.

atoms.a: Ashley is driving a car. Her brother Tom is riding a horse. Who would win the race?

text: A sailing boat sails with wind. It has a mast and a triangular sail which catches the wind and makes the boat move.

instruction.text: Listen and read along, then select the correct answer by using the information from the graph.

atoms.a: Mariah is on holiday in Greece. She wants to take a slow and relaxing boat-ride to visit some beautiful islands. Which boat should she take?

instruction.text: Listen and read along, then select the correct answer by using the information from the graph.

atoms.a: Peter lives in Devon and wants to visit his best friend in Newcastle. He knows the distance from Devon to Newcastle is pretty far, but he is sure that going by train is faster than flying. Is he correct?
